title: Lone distinctions in the weave: what is proved, and what is sketched
claim: T (proved): two knots sharing two distinctions leave their lone, facing, opposite-class distinctions unbonded. H and L (the advisor's sketches, checked computationally): on weave patches without holes a set is constrained exactly when m >= 3 of its members have a cyclic order of height-distance sum at most 3(m - 2); D(x,y) + D(y,x) = 3 steps; hence b >= steps + 1 on every such patch. Open: the upper bound (false in 64 pairs, ticket B) and which facing pairs are bonded. Refereed R1: the computed reading 'a patch fails exactly when some pair is unbonded' is blocked beyond eleven knots (a facing lone pair can fail bonded, at steps + 3); H, L and the lower bound are proved in WEAVE-HEIGHTS-20261118-001A.
standard_statement: Triangular Ising antiferromagnet height functions (Bloete-Hilhorst 1982; Nienhuis-Hilhorst-Bloete 1984); heights as difference constraints (Thurston 1990); systolic complexes.
completion_gate: Ticket B's gates and frozen census; the referee reviews the proofs and sketches.

validation.status: T proved; H and L sketched here, proved in WEAVE-HEIGHTS-20261118-001A; refereed R1 (one reading blocked)
validation.independence: brute-force solution sets and computed readings against the statements; same task authorship
validation.novelty: the height mapping classical; the lone-pair obstruction not known to the advisor (no literature search run)

attained_result: T proved; H, L and the lower bound sketched and checked computationally; census in ticket B.
